title: Вердикт комиссии и транс Макса  (The Commission's Verdict and Max's Trance)

segments.t: At the commission's dinner table, the chairwoman declares that Hotel Eleon deserves only three stars because the service is a nightmare. To win a vote in their favor, Chef Barinov sits behind the unconscious Pavel Vladimirovich and puppets his head while the hypnotist puts Max into a trance.
Мой вердикт — три звезды.
Сервис, персонал — это кошмар какой-то!
Кому ещё вина?
Вкусно. Павел Владимирович, а вы что думаете?
Понятно. Я, конечно, согласен с вами.
Но с другой стороны, в целом отель неплохой.
Персонал старается.
Я сейчас.
Всё понравилось?
Очень.
Что-то он долго. Она его в транс вводит!
Ничего, Макс с детства не поддаётся гипнозу.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Мой вердикт — три звезды.
'My verdict is three stars.' In Russian, the idea of 'my' flows naturally into 'stars' without extra filler words.
Сервис, персонал — это кошмар какой-то!
'The service, the staff, it is some kind of nightmare!' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'service' and finishing on 'some kind of'.
Кому ещё вина?
'More wine for anyone?' Notice how Russian expresses 'to whom' and 'wine' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. the inspector answers right away.
Вкусно. Павел Владимирович, а вы что думаете?
'Delicious. Pavel Vladimirovich, and what do you think?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'deliciously' and finishing on 'think'.
Понятно. Я, конечно, согласен с вами.
'Understood. I, of course, agree with you.' The meaning hinges on 'understood' working together with 'you' in spoken Russian.
Но с другой стороны, в целом отель неплохой.
'But on the other hand, overall the hotel is not bad.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'but', while 'not bad' completes the thought.
Персонал старается.
'The staff tries hard.' Chef Barinov brings out the contrast between 'staff' and 'tries hard' in a few short words.
Я сейчас.
'I will be right back.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'now' in spoken Russian.
Всё понравилось?
'Did you like everything?' In Russian, the idea of 'everything' flows naturally into 'pleased' without extra filler words. the inspector answers right away.
Очень.
'Very much.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'very' and finishing on 'very'.
Что-то он долго. Она его в транс вводит!
'He is taking a long time. She is putting him into a trance!' The grammar packs 'something' and 'puts into' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Ничего, Макс с детства не поддаётся гипнозу.

'It is nothing, Max has not succumbed to hypnosis since childhood.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'nothing' and finishing on 'hypnosis'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

That brings the dining-room scene to a close. Notice how the chairwoman announces her three-star verdict while Kostya realizes the woman is putting Max into a trance. See you next time!
До завтра!
